title: Centre-out heirloom blanket
subtitle: A 90 cm square blanket knitted from the centre out in four lace sections.
excerpt: A 90 cm square heirloom blanket worked from the centre out in four quadrants simultaneously on two circular needles or a long circular using the magic-loop method. Each quadrant builds from a four-stitch cast-on at the centre with paired increases. A lace vine repeat decorates each quadrant. About 350 g of DK. ADVANCED: four simultaneous live sections, centre increases, and lace on all four needles.
sourceNotes: Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971), §Pi Shawl and Centre-Out Construction, describes knitting outward from a centre cast-on as a classic technique for square shawls and blankets. Weldon's Practical Knitter, 1st series (1885), §Knitted Squares, gives a centre-start square blanket with garter increases.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. Each quadrant grows by 2 stitches every RS row (yo before and after centre spine); finished blanket is 90 cm × 90 cm square.

Pre-cast-off check — 400 sts total (100 per section)

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitting method where the work begins with a very small number of stitches at the exact centre of the piece and grows outward by paired increases at each section boundary. For a square, four sections grow simultaneously from a four-stitch (or eight-stitch) centre, with increases at the inner corners of each quadrant. The finished piece grows from the inside out, which means the edge is always the active knitting row.

content.text: A 90 cm square blanket knitted by
centre-out construction
on 4 mm needles. Four quadrants grow from an eight-stitch centre. Each RS row adds two stitches per quadrant. A simple vine lace repeat fills each quadrant.

The technique is ADVANCED because four sections are live simultaneously, each must be tracked independently for the lace repeat and for the paired increase placement, and the centre becomes a permanent visual focal point where any tension or alignment error will be visible. The reward is a blanket with no seams and a radiating design that is inherently oriented from the centre outward. Budget about 350 g (about 770 m / 842 yards) of DK. Wet blocking is non-optional; the centre-out structure does not relax naturally into a flat square without it.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 350 g (about 770 m / 842 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn. A smooth plied DK in a solid colour shows the lace clearly.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 100 cm or longer (centre-out requires a long cable or two circulars)

items.name: Blocking mat and pins
items.qty: Required, the square cannot be held flat without blocking

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. At this gauge, reaching 90 cm from the centre requires 99 RS rows of increases (each RS row adds 2 stitches per quadrant), giving 100 stitches per quadrant and 400 total stitches at cast-off. If your gauge is 20 per 10 cm, the same 99 rows produce a blanket about 99 cm across.
Stitches used

items.name: yo
items.qty: yarn over (used as a paired increase at each section boundary)

content.text: Pattern
Centre cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 8 stitches (2 stitches per quadrant). Long-tail tail: (4 × 8) / 10 + 15 = 3.2 + 15 = 18.2 cm. Measure 25 cm. Join for working flat by dividing: place 2 stitches per quadrant onto the needle with a marker between each group (4 markers total).
Increase rows (plain garter base, rows 1 to 10)
RS increase row: *yo, k to 1 st before marker, yo, SM, k1; repeat from * 3 more times. (+8 sts total per RS row, +2 per quadrant)
WS rows: k all. Work 10 increase rows to establish the centre garter square before introducing lace.
Lace vine body (from row 11 onward)

RS increase rows: *yo, [vine lace repeat: k3, yo, k2tog, k1, ssk, yo] across quadrant, yo, SM, k1; repeat for all 4 quadrants. The vine repeat is 8 stitches and must be worked in full repeats only; adjust to k plain for partial repeats at the section edges. WS rows: p all within each quadrant, k the marker spine stitches.

Continue increasing every RS row and working the vine repeat within each quadrant as it grows. When a quadrant becomes wide enough to hold 2 complete vine repeats (16 stitches), add the second repeat; until then, work the partial section as stocking stitch. Set this aside noting the RS row count and the vine position within each quadrant.
Stitch count check-ins

At RS row 99 (about 45 cm from centre, about 90 cm diagonally): count across all four quadrants. You should have 204 total stitches (51 per quadrant). At RS row 197 (about 89 cm from centre): count again. You should have 400 stitches (100 per quadrant).
Common faults
Centre puckering: the cast-on tension is too tight at the original 8 stitches. Work the first 4 increase rows very loosely and block the centre firmly when finishing.

Vine lace misaligning between quadrants: each quadrant starts its vine repeat on a different RS row because the repeat count does not enter all four sections simultaneously. Treat each quadrant as an independent entity; do not try to synchronise them.

Blanket ruffling at the outer edge: the increases are too frequent relative to the stitch gauge. Check that each RS row is only adding 2 stitches per quadrant (not 4 or 6), and confirm gauge matches 22 stitches per 10 cm.
Cast-off
Cast off all 400 stitches knitwise with needles one size larger and a relaxed tension. The cast-off edge must be elastic to accept blocking.
Finishing

Soak the finished piece thoroughly. Pin to a 90 × 90 cm square on blocking mats: start at the four corners and extend the cast-off edge outward to the marked dimensions. Pin the centre firmly. The centre puckering and ruffle, if any, disappear under careful blocking. Leave to dry fully.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, reshaping to a square.
What to try next

From a centre-out DK blanket, try a centre-out Shetland lace shawl in 4-ply. The four-section construction is the same. The gauge is finer. The lace repeat grows to 32 rows. A knitted-on border is worked sideways and grafted on at the end.
